history.sg_progress: The model forms of contracts developed by the Office of Legal Affairs for the purchase of goods, for the acquisition of services and for obtaining both goods and related services stipulate that the United Nations has no obligation to provide any assistance to the contractor providing the goods or performing the services other than as expressly agreed and set forth in the applicable contract. The United Nations makes no representations as to the availability of any facilities or equipment that may be helpful to or useful for the contractor’s performance. Thus, the United Nations model contracts stipulate, in general, that the United Nations contractor is responsible, at its own cost, for providing all necessary personnel, equipment, material and supplies, and for making all arrangements necessary for its performance under the contract. As a legal matter, all contracts signed by representatives of the United Nations must clearly set forth the obligations of each of the parties, in order to ensure clarity under the contract and legal certainty. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if a United Nations contract includes a provision requiring the United Nations to provide some assistance or support to the contractor, then the Organization should ensure that it meets its contractual obligations under the contract. With regard to a certain mission that was mentioned by the Board, the Administration requests the closure of this recommendation since the United Nations and the contractor have reached a settlement that is favourable to the United Nations.
